subject: Buyout & suspension clauses — prepay matrix and mid-term true-up
messages:
From: Aisha Khatri <aisha.khatri@kineticretail.com>

Cc: procurement@kineticretail.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prepay structure questions — buyout & suspension concerns

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the pricing model you sent last week. Procurement has two specific concerns before we can move to legal:

- If we prepay for year 2 and then materially under-deliver (our traffic ramps 40% lower than plan), what recourse do we have? Is there a mid-term true-up or partial refund mechanism?
- We need clarity on a buyout (customer-initiated early exit). If we commit to 36 months with an upfront payment, what is the termination schedule and how would refunds be calculated?

We'd also like to understand suspension language (if we pause usage for a quarter, does the prepay get held in escrow, amortized, or forfeit?).

Attached: high-level procurement checklist and our expected ramp profile.

Can your team propose concrete contract language/terms we can share with counsel?

Best,
Aisha
Procurement Manager
KineticRetail Inc.

Attachment: Kinetic_RFP_Ramp_Profile.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prepay structure questions — buyout & suspension concerns

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. I pulled Marcus (pricing) and Ben (legal ops) in to propose an operationally simple matrix that addresses each ask. High-level proposals below; we can put draft language in the contract after you confirm the direction.

1) Mid-term true-up / ramp variance
- Principle: protect both parties. If actual monthly usage in any quarter is below forecast by >25%, we propose a quarterly true-up where the shortfall is credited against future months (not cashed back), with a one-time optional refund at milestone endpoints (yearly).
- Mechanics: shortfall_credit = prepaid_monthly_charge * months_underperforming * (1 - scale_factor). Scale factor tiers (see attachment): 25–50% shortfall -> 60% refundable credit; >50% -> 80% refundable credit. Credits applied against future invoices first.

2) Buyout / early termination (customer-initiated)
- Proposal A (standard): pro rata refund of unconsumed prepaid balance less a 15% early-exit fee; refunds issued on a 90-day processing cycle.
- Proposal B (accelerator): for 36-month deals with >30% upfront prepay, allow a reduced fee of 8% but require 60-day notice and waiver of any pending credits.

3) Suspension (temporary pause)
- Short suspensions (<=90 days): put prepaid balance into escrow; amortize remaining monthly value once usage resumes.
- Long suspensions (>90 days): option to convert prepaid balance to a hold credit that expires 12 months from suspension start, or trigger a partial refund per schedule (25% at 180 days, 50% at 12 months).

Attachments: I attached a worked example matrix (Kinetic_TrueUp_Template.xlsx) and draft redline snippets (Draft_SLA_and_ATA_redlines.pdf). 

If you like this direction, Ben can surface contract language for each bullet and we can run numbers on your ramp profile.

Next steps: if procurement agrees to the approach, we'll prepare two clean options (A and B) for counsel review.

Thanks — Soojin
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Kinetic_TrueUp_Template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), Draft_SLA_and_ATA_redlines.pdf (pdf stub)

Soojin,

Thanks — appreciate the options. Procurement prefers a path that preserves their ability to get cash refunds if the product materially underperforms (they have internal stakeholder constraints). Two follow-ups:

- Can you provide the cash-refund dollar example for our 36-month, $1.2M upfront scenario under both Proposal A and Proposal B? We want the net cash returned after early-exit fee.
- For suspension: they are especially worried about long-term holds (12+ months). Would Redwood consider a time-bound escrow release so that any unused prepaid after 12 months is auto-refunded at a pre-agreed amortization rate?

If you can get concrete numbers and the exact contract clause language, we'll get counsel to review quickly.

Best,
Aisha

(Attachment: Kinetic_Ramp_Profile.xlsx updated)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prepay structure questions — buyout & suspension concerns

Hi Aisha — Marcus here (pricing). I ran the $1.2M upfront against both proposals and attached a worked example in the spreadsheet (sheet: BuyoutExamples). Summary:

- Proposal A (15% fee): refund = remaining_unconsumed_balance - 15% fee. For your expected consumption through month 18 (we modeled 55% of committed tokens used), remaining_unconsumed_balance = $540,000 -> refund ~= $459,000 (after 15% = $81,000).
- Proposal B (8% fee, conditions): refund ~= $496,800 (after 8% = $43,200) but only if you accept the accelerator terms (60-day notice, waiver of pending credits).

Suspension auto-refund: We can agree to an auto-refund trigger at the 12-month suspension mark. Operationally that would be: place funds in escrow at suspension start; at 12 months, calculate unused balance and refund per amortization schedule (we propose straight-line amortization minus a 5% escrow handling fee).

Proposed contract snippets (high level):
- Early Termination: "Upon Customer early termination, Redwood will calculate the unconsumed prepaid balance and issue refund net of Early Exit Fee (15% standard, 8% if Accelerator terms are met)."
- Suspension: "Upon suspension exceeding 90 days, funds will be placed into escrow. If suspension continues beyond 12 months, remaining escrowed funds will be refunded per amortization schedule less a 5% handling fee unless Customer elects credit conversion."

Ben — can you draft the exact language for legal review (I'll mark up the attached pdf).

Aisha — if both summaries look right, we'll convert these into two marked-up contract options and share a DocuSign link for the option you prefer.

Thanks — Marcus
Director, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Kinetic_TrueUp_Template.xlsx (updated sheets: BuyoutExamples)

  - Option B: Accelerator (8% fee) with 60-day notice, no pending-credit claims, and slightly higher minimum commit language

2) Suspension handling: escrow at suspension start; auto-refund at 12 months per straight-line amortization minus 5% handling fee. We'll add an explicit conversion-to-credit option.
